initrd.whyUnused: the guest kernel has virtio-blk and ext4 built in rather than as modules, so it can reach the sealed root filesystem without one. The initrd carries the same tree as a cpio archive and has no /init, so using it would mean adding a boot path this image was not built for.

whatFailed.cause: The root filesystem has no mount-point directories for the kernel's virtual filesystems. Its top level holds usr, etc, opt, var, boot and the usr-merge symlinks and nothing else, so there is no /proc, /sys or /dev for PID 1 to mount over.
notTheCause: Not the boot loader: the kernel ran and handed over to init.
Not the image's determinism: the same bytes both replicas produced were read here.
Not the missing account database: systemd froze before reaching any user lookup.
whatFailed.observed: systemd started as PID 1 and stopped before identifying itself: it could not mount /proc, /sys or /dev, each failing with No such file or directory, and then printed Freezing execution. The frozen marker for this condition is a systemd[1]: log line, which systemd emits only after those mounts exist.

whatWorked: The kernel started from the sealed image, with no initrd, on Virtualization.framework.
virtio-blk presented the sealed disk as /dev/vda at its exact size, 2281864 512-byte blocks.
The ext4 filesystem mounted read-only from that device and the kernel reported the root mounted.
The kernel executed /usr/lib/systemd/systemd as its init process, so the path and the binary are both real.
The sealed image hashed identically before and after, so the read-only attachment held.
whatWouldBeNeeded: A new guest image whose builder creates the empty mount-point directories, and with it the /run and /tmp the same startup needs. That is a new production of the root disk, which the standing instruction allows exactly once and has already spent, so it requires a separate operator approval before it may be produced or booted again.
